topIssues.title: kona-interop: Review access of blocks created internally
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
Currently when Kona-proofs interop performs the interop validation step, if the first validation pass identifies blocks that need to be replaced, it builds them and sets them as chain head then does another validation pass to see if that has caused other chains to become invalid.  But in the second pass it loads the deposit-only block it just generated from the preimage oracle. This block will be canonical so the load will work, but given the block was just built this is a suspicious design choice.

If it ever asks the preimage oracle from a block that isn't canonical (eg an optimistic block it just derived which is later replaced), it would cause failures.  We should review for safety and consider prioritising first checking if the block is already known before loading from the oracle.

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Prune Denylist on L1 Reorg and Alert
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
We need to ensure that whenever the Virtual Node responds to an L1 reorg, all downstream components prune data:

Chain Containers must prune their `Denylist` - if not, then a legitimate Unsafe chain could be denied inappropriately

Activities need to be notified via the same `Reset` callback already used. This is because they need to prune their verification results and logs.
Related: Related to: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19287

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Prune Interop Database on L1 Reorg
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
Currently, when the L1 reorgs, there is no attempt from the interop activity to remove old data.

The individual virtual nodes will respond to reorgs, and that in turn will clear out the individual log databases and verification data. However, if L1 inconsistency is not understood by the supernode, it could potentially represent situations where some virtual nodes are on a divergent L1 view.

Note that this is exceedingly unlikely in an application sense because all Virtual Nodes share an L1 connection. However, if an L1 were to reorg as logs were collected, an inconsistent view of that particular timestamp could be constructed. This would cause a "Safe" view of the data which is hiding inconsistency.

To address this, we should slightly expand the CurrentL1 tracking to:
- Confirm CurrentL1 values are all canonical with one-another
- Confirm L1 values did not change during the operation

Some of this consistency checking is already done in the interop activity.


Far-Future Note:
Many of the operational patterns of tracking the CurrentL1 and providing L2 timestamped data are generic to all Verification Activities. Therefore, many of the structs and runtime patterns in it SHOULD be moved upward so that each VA can feature a minimal definition of how to setup and run. Not the purpose of this ticket, but as we think about ensuring L1 consistency, we should consider that actually this could be supplied at a level above activities themselves.

topPRs.title: sc-feat: policy engine staking ordering
topPRs.author: ashitakah
topPRs.body:
**PolicyEngineStaking** is a periphery contract that enables stake-aware transaction ordering in op-rbuilder.

Users deposit OP tokens and optionally link their stake to a beneficiary that receives ordering power. The contract maintains an aggregated, PE-optimized view of effective stake and last update timestamp per address in a single packed storage slot, allowing the Policy Engine to read stake data directly via state_by_block_hash() with O(1) lookups and no RPC calls.

topPRs.title: op-devstack: add capability interfaces for polymorphic lookups (Phase 3)
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
This PR introduces capability interfaces for op-devstack that enable polymorphic lookups across component types with different ID signatures. This is Phase 3 of the ID type system refactor.

### Problem

Components like `RollupBoostNode` and `OPRBuilderNode` provide L2 EL functionality but can't implement `L2ELNode` because their `ID()` methods return different types:

```go
// L2ELNode has: ID() L2ELNodeID
// RollupBoostNode has: ID() RollupBoostNodeID
// OPRBuilderNode has: ID() OPRBuilderNodeID
```

This forced manual multi-registry lookups:

```go
func (o *Orchestrator) GetL2EL(id stack.L2ELNodeID) (L2ELNode, bool) {
    if el, ok := o.l2ELs.Get(id); ok {
        return el, true
    }
    rbID := stack.NewRollupBoostNodeID(id.Key(), id.ChainID())
    if rb, ok := o.rollupBoosts.Get(rbID); ok {
        return rb, true
    }
    // ... check OPRBuilder too
}
```

### Solution

Capability interfaces capture shared behavior without the incompatible `ID()` method:

```go
type L2ELCapable interface {
    L2EthClient() apis.L2EthClient
    L2EngineClient() apis.EngineClient
    ELNode
}
```

Polymorphic lookup by key:

```go
sequencer, ok := FindL2ELCapableByKey(registry, "sequencer", chainID)
// Returns whichever L2ELCapable component has that key
```

### Changes

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `stack/capabilities.go` | L2ELCapable interface and registry helpers |
| `stack/capabilities_test.go` | Comprehensive test suite (9 tests) |
| [Design document](https://www.notion.so/oplabs/Devstack-ID-Type-System-Refactor-2eef153ee1628048bb7ade1030fe6e9b) | Phase 3 implementation notes |

### Test Plan

- [x] `L2ELCapableKinds()` returns expected kinds
- [x] `RegistryFindByCapability` finds all implementing components
- [x] `RegistryFindByCapabilityOnChain` filters by chain
- [x] `FindL2ELCapableByKey` polymorphic lookup works
- [x] `FindL2ELCapableByKey` prefers L2ELNode when multiple types share a key
- [x] Polymorphic scenario test demonstrates the use case

dependency set contains only one L2 chain. This covers both preinterop

scenarios using op-supernode.
